entrypoints.summary: A local actor able to modify the victim user's application files accesses the regular-install archive at C:\Users\<Username>\AppData\Local\1Password\app\8\resources\app.asar.

affected_components.role: Report-described packaged Electron UI resources and injected script; no application source snapshot is supplied.

causal_paths.kind: packaged-resource modification to UI-context script execution

negative_controls: The report identifies the enterprise MSI installation in Program Files as not affected.
No supplied artifact contains an independent execution trace or a verified fixed-build test result.
observability.positive_marker: An alert(1) dialog appears after the altered application is started.

preconditions: The actor has local malware/file-write capability in the victim user's profile.
The target uses the report-described regular Windows installation location rather than the Program Files enterprise MSI installation.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: An added JavaScript file loaded through <script src="backdoor.js"></script>; alert(1) is the documented execution probe, and document.getElementById('root').innerText is the documented UI-read operation.
trigger_steps.summary: Unpack app.asar, add backdoor.js, insert a script reference in primary.html, repack app.asar, and open the application.

sources.concept: local malware with write access to user-profile application files

impact.affected_asset: Revealed password data in the 1Password application's UI, plus integrity of packaged Electron HTML/JavaScript resources.
impact.attacker_capability: A local same-user malware actor can persistently backdoor the regular-install application archive and extract UI-displayed unlocked-password content after launch.
impact.security_effect: Attacker-controlled JavaScript executes in the 1Password UI context and can read unlocked passwords that are revealed in the UI.

causal_trace.summary: Local malware can modify the regular-install Electron files because 1Password is installed under the user's local application directory rather than a trusted folder.
Executable HTML and JavaScript packaged in app.asar do not retain code integrity against a principal that can write the user-profile installation path.
The documented procedure unpacks app.asar, adds backdoor.js, references it from primary.html, and repacks the modified archive before application launch.

On application opening, Electron executes the injected JavaScript; the report uses alert(1) as the execution observation and states that script can read the root element's innerText to obtain revealed passwords.

failure.operation: Electron loads the attacker-modified primary.html and executes the added backdoor.js when 1Password is opened.

primary_invariant.statement: Application HTML and JavaScript resources must be installed in a location that a same-user unprivileged malware process cannot modify.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The regular Windows installation stores app.asar in the user's Local AppData directory, where the report demonstrates unpacking, altering, and repacking executable Electron UI resources.

raw_refs.role: primary audit finding, reproduction procedure, and remediation response

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report gives a concrete reproduction procedure and reports alert(1) as an execution observation, but the bundle contains no independently runnable harness, execution log, application source snapshot, exact affected product version, or public fix commit. The report describes protected-install work and an unaffected enterprise MSI, not confirmed rollout of a final fix. The prerequisite is local malware/file-modification capability; this record does not treat the finding as initial remote code execution.

remediation.invariant_restored: Place the application in a safe protected location such as Program Files, requiring elevation/UAC as appropriate, so basic malware able to write the user profile cannot alter its packaged executable UI resources.
mitigation_classes: installer-mediated write protection for executable resources

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Attacker already has local malware capability sufficient to modify files in the victim user's Local AppData profile; the report directs terminating 1Password before archive modification.
data_structure_invariants: app.asar must contain application resources whose executable HTML/JavaScript cannot be altered by the local user-profile writer.
The UI root's text content becomes sensitive when passwords are revealed.
state_context.state_machine: terminated application -> attacker modifies and repacks app.asar -> application opens -> injected script executes -> passwords may be revealed in UI and read by the script

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Windows regular installation assessed by Cure53 in late 2021; exact product build/version is not identified in the supplied report.

target.component: Electron app.asar archive and primary.html UI resources
target.language: HTML/JavaScript (Electron packaged UI resources; application language otherwise not established by this finding)
